title: xDiT parallelism: separate current-state attention from stale-state pipelines
summary: USP, CFG splitting and PipeFusion have different topology, memory and quality tradeoffs; qualify each before combining them.

hardware: Multiple CUDA GPUs with recorded interconnect topology; model support is method-specific
software: xdit-project/xDiT at f7c16aa958379a9f0a0302350fe0e1bfcec5f23c; later revisions need reinspection
conditions: A supported diffusion pipeline and compatible sequence/head partitioning
Record CFG setting, denoising schedule and all parallel degrees

claims.description: USP combines Ulysses and Ring sequence parallelism. CFG parallelism splits the two guidance branches when CFG is active.
The source cost table labels Ulysses/Ring attention data as fresh and PipeFusion as using stale information. PipeFusion requires serial warmup steps that affect its benefit.

downstream_impact: vLLM-Omni: compare sequence partition choices using exposed communication and memory, not only rank count.
Treat PipeFusion as a separate quality-sensitive experiment, particularly for few-step/distilled models where warmup consumes much of the schedule.
vllm-ascend: transfer topology reasoning only after independently checking collectives, rank ownership and numerical behavior.
recommendations: Treat downstream impact as an OmniRSI transfer hypothesis, not an upstream compatibility or performance result.
validation_plan: Measure denoise and whole-generation latency, communication overlap, per-rank memory and scaling under fixed model/seed/shape/steps.
Evaluate output quality for each method and combination; test uneven token/head layouts and disabled CFG.
limitations: Backend-specific implementations and model matrices do not transfer with the high-level method.
Current-state attention still requires numerical validation; stale-state methods must not be advertised as lossless from a speed benchmark.
Point-in-time source extraction, not a historical commit-delta audit. No local accelerator or model-quality reproduction was run.
